question: Should OpenClaw adopt this centralized, fail-closed localization coverage manifest and repository-wide validation gate as core governance, rather than keeping localization maturity and ownership checks surface-local or advisory?
rationale: The patch establishes durable cross-product policy, a closed inventory of owned surfaces, and a required validation gate; implementation quality alone cannot determine whether that governance boundary matches maintainer product direction.

options.title: Sponsor the centralized governance model
options.body: Approve the manifest and required gate in principle, then require the series to be restacked and demonstrated with real after-fix evidence.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Keep localized contributor guidance but limit the inventory and checks to currently migrated surfaces or non-blocking reporting until ownership is established.

options.title: Keep governance surface-local
options.body: Decline the central manifest direction and retain validation in the individual UI, CLI, native, and documentation owners.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the centralized governance model
recommendation.body: Approve the manifest and required gate in principle, then require the series to be restacked and demonstrated with real after-fix evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: They can clarify the series design and intended boundary; maintainer sponsorship remains required for the actual product decision.
